---
title: Plugin record and health
---

A plugin registers one record, an `lk.Plugin`, under the entry-point group `laplacekit.plugins`.
The entry name is the import package:

```toml
[project.entry-points."laplacekit.plugins"]
laplacekit_transformers = "laplacekit_transformers:plugin"
```

The last lines of `laplacekit_transformers` are its checks and its record:

```python
def health() -> tuple[lk.HealthCheck, ...]:
    """Check for `lk.health()` that `transformers` is installed, and `peft` if possible."""

    checks = [_installed("transformers", "error", "required")]
    checks += [
        _installed(dist, "warning", f"optional, for {use}") for dist, use in _OPTIONAL.items()
    ]

    return tuple(checks)


plugin = lk.Plugin(supports=">=0.1a0,<0.2", health=health)
```

That is all the registration there is.
Importing a plugin has no side effects and changes no defaults.
The record is read only when `lk.plugins()` or `lk.health()` runs.

## `supports`

`supports` is a [PEP 440](https://peps.python.org/pep-0440/#version-specifiers) specifier set: the **laplacekit** versions the plugin works with.
Pre-releases count, so `">=0.1a0,<0.2"` takes the current alpha.
The API changes between minor versions until 1.0, so an upper bound at the next minor version is a safe default.
A plugin outside its range still loads, but `lk.plugins()` marks it "not supported" and `lk.health()` reports an error.

## `lk.plugins()`

`lk.plugins()` lists every installed plugin.
The name, version and summary come from the package metadata (the summary is `description` in `pyproject.toml`).
Under them come the names in the plugin module's `__all__`, each with the first line of its docstring, so that line should say what the object is.
The record and `health` are left out.
A plugin that fails to import is listed with the error.
[Your first plugin](first.py) prints the list.

## `lk.health()`

`lk.health()` checks the install.
It runs the core's checks first (the torch version, the `curvlinops` pin, a probe of a small model, float64), then, for each plugin, a `supports` check and the plugin's own `health()`.

`health` takes no arguments and returns a tuple of `lk.HealthCheck`.
Each check has a name, a status and a short detail:

- `"ok"`: works.
- `"warning"`: works, with something missing, e.g., an optional dependency.
- `"error"`: broken.

A `health` that raises shows up as one error check naming the exception, so `lk.health()` itself never fails because of a plugin.
The default `health` returns no checks; a plugin without a dependency of its own, such as the one in [Your first plugin](first.py), can leave it out.
A good check is cheap and real: the version of the library the plugin wraps, as `laplacekit-transformers` reports, and a fit of a tiny model.
[Using a plugin](../quickstart/plugins.py) prints a full report.
